items.event_time_ist: Monday, Oct 19 (during a training exercise); toll updated Tuesday, Oct 20
items.summary: Three ballistic missiles struck the Martyr Ahmed al-Sulaimani Training Centre at al-Alam camp in Shabwa province while recruits were lining up for a training session. Provincial governor Awad al-Wazir raised the death toll from 53 to 73 on Tuesday, with 200+ injured and 14 missing; hospitals in Shabwa were overwhelmed and the critically wounded were moved to Hadramout and Aden. AP called it the deadliest Houthi attack since the group resumed large-scale operations in July; Reuters verified video of bodies scattered across the camp. Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree claimed the camp was run by Saudi forces; Yemen's Information Minister called the training centre a non-legitimate target and a war crime.
items.title: Houthi missile strike on Shabwa training camp kills 73 — deadliest since July

items.event_time_ist: Reopened Sat, Oct 17; recovery update Tue, Oct 20
items.source_name: The National via Airways Magazine / Gulf Business
items.summary: King Khalid International Airport reopened after its week-long closure, but GACA NOTAM A3650/26 (effective 18:45 UTC Oct 17, no expiry) still requires airlines to obtain prior permission for every arrival and departure. The recovery has stalled: Emirates reversed its planned Oct 20-21 restart (EK815/817/819 cancelled), Air France-KLM pushed Riyadh off through Nov 7, Etihad through Oct 24, Akasa Air through Oct 27, Lufthansa until Nov 18, and Gulf Air is still suspended. On Oct 19, 181 of 274 scheduled Riyadh departures (66%) were cancelled or listed no-fly; Cirium counts 45.5% of all Saudi departures disrupted since Oct 8.
items.title: Riyadh airport reopened Oct 17 — but recovery stalled, most carriers still grounded

items.source_name: DPA/Qatar Tribune via British Columbia Times
items.summary: Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki announced interceptions across three days: on Oct 17 four drones launched toward Riyadh were destroyed; on Oct 18 two ballistic missiles aimed at Khamis Mushait were intercepted along with two drones near the capital and a third drone over the oil-rich east. Saudi MoD separately confirmed the Oct 18 intercept of two ballistic missiles and a UAV. Maliki denied a Houthi claim of downing a Saudi Apache attack helicopter. No damage or casualty figures were released for these interceptions.
items.title: Coalition reports fresh interceptions Oct 17-19: drones over Riyadh, missiles at Khamis Mushait

items.summary: Coalition spokesman Maliki said a Saudi AH-6i reconnaissance helicopter crashed in Najran near the Yemeni border due to a technical malfunction, killing both crew members. Separately, Saudi civil defense reported that six people were injured when a hostile projectile struck a residential neighborhood in Najran, damaging three homes and three vehicles. Fox News also reported that Riyadh's iconic Kingdom Centre sent workers home amid the attacks, underscoring the capital's jittery state despite the airport reopening.
items.title: Saudi helicopter crashes in Najran (2 crew killed); projectile hits Najran homes, 6 hurt

items.event_time_ist: Sat–Mon, Oct 17–19; vote postponed to next Monday
items.summary: President Sisi told a military academy ceremony on Oct 17 that Egypt would take 'any measures necessary' to defend Saudi Arabia if asked, and requested an emergency parliament session to authorize military assistance. The presidency then said Cairo was ready to give 'all necessary and possible support' to defend Saudi security, stability, territorial integrity and holy sites, following a National Defence Council meeting. Parliament held the emergency session on Sunday but postponed the authorization vote to next Monday; Sisi stressed any mission would be defensive and only proceed if Riyadh asks.
items.title: Egypt's Sisi seeks parliament authorization to defend Saudi Arabia; vote postponed

items.summary: Organizers postponed next week's 10th edition of the Future Investment Initiative ('Davos in the Desert'), saying the decision was taken to preserve the event's scale and quality. It joins other modified/cancelled events: the EU-GCC summit, Riyadh Fashion Week, the Six Kings Slam tennis tournament and the PIF Saudi International golf tournament. The same reporting disclosed the kingdom's aggregate tally: the Houthis hit Riyadh airport with 20 projectiles (10 drones, 4 ballistic missiles, 4 cruise missiles, 2 unidentified) over the past two weeks — 13 killed and 300+ injured in one strike, 5 more killed and dozens injured in the others.
items.title: Saudi postpones 'Davos in the Desert' FII; golf, tennis, fashion week also hit

items.summary: Yahya Saree claimed six operations against Saudi targets in 48 hours: King Khalid airport (Riyadh), Aramco facilities in Yanbu, the Shaybah oil field, Abha airport, radar installations, Khamis Mushait airbase, a Saudi naval camp and a radar site near Bir Askar — described as 'precise and direct.' He said the operations retaliate for more than 200 coalition airstrikes and missile attacks on Houthi-held territory in the same period and vowed continued escalation until attacks on Yemen stop. None of these strikes has been independently verified or acknowledged by Saudi authorities.
items.title: Saree claims six operations in 48 hours: Riyadh airport, Yanbu, Shaybah, Abha
